question: 035-037: does continuous production plus contemporaneous weather explain remaining mean/max differences?
joint_support: For June vs each later month, same clock hour and wet status; all four continuous standardized differences <=1 June SD, nearest opposite-month observation. Keep only hour cells with >=5 eligible observations each month.
sensitivity: inverse-profile weights and leave-one-calendar-week-out, fixed covariate transformation; repeated-data exploratory association, no iid p-values
missing_handling_after_diagnostic: First fit failed because June 1 hours 1 and 2 have missing wind, previously documented EDA missingness. Use the same 1242 complete cases for all four models; retain original data and all 1244 rows in distribution analysis, no imputation.
followup_after_first_results: Weather addition changes monthly contrasts. Diagnose each weather group's unique in-sample association by omitting that block from the same fixed joint model, not selecting variables. Drop only exactly all-zero spline basis columns, record names, and recheck rank; no information-bearing variable removed.
stop: If support gate fails, no adjusted full-period attribution. Calendar/production/weather/joint fits remain descriptive same-sample relationships, not future predictive evaluation or causal contributions.
